outcomeTiers.explanation: You navigated something genuinely difficult without losing yourself, or either friendship, in the process. That's rarer than it sounds.
It got messy, but you came through with both friendships more or less intact — bruised, not broken.
You stayed neutral when neutral wasn't really available. Something in one of these friendships is going to take a while to settle.
You said the easy thing every time it mattered, and it cost you the trust of someone who needed you to be honest.

start.message: Jordan catches you alone in the kitchen after everyone else has drifted off. Their voice is lower than usual. "Can I tell you something? I just... need you not to judge me before I've even said it."

data.location: Kitchen, after everyone else has left

choices.label: Of course. Whatever it is, I'm listening.

reasons.savvy: You read that Jordan needed to feel safe before they could be honest.
reasons.streetSmarts: Meeting someone with openness usually earns you the real story, not a filtered one.
reasons.integrity: Offering that before you even know what's coming is its own kind of trust.

reasons.streetSmarts: Conditional listening tends to get a conditional, guarded answer back.

confession.message: Jordan takes a breath. "I kissed someone. At the work conference last month. It's over — it happened once, I ended it immediately, I haven't spoken to them since. I just... I can't lose Alex over this. Please don't say anything."

choices.label: I won't say anything — but you need to tell Alex yourself, and soon.

reasons.savvy: You separated 'I'll keep your confidence' from 'I'll help you hide this' — those aren't the same thing.
reasons.streetSmarts: You held the line without becoming the messenger between two people.
reasons.integrity: You didn't just promise silence — you named what actually needs to happen.

choices.label: How could you do that to Alex?

reasons.savvy: Your reaction was honest, even if it wasn't what Jordan needed to hear in that moment.
reasons.streetSmarts: Leading with judgment when someone's already frightened tends to shut a conversation down rather than open it up.
reasons.integrity: Not pretending to be fine with it is its own kind of honesty.

reveal_calm.message: Weeks later, Alex pulls you aside, grinning, unable to keep it in. "I'm going to propose. To Jordan. I want your help picking the place — and I need it to be a total surprise." You still haven't fully processed what Jordan told you, but Alex is watching your face, waiting for you to be as excited as they are.

choices.label: That's incredible. Of course I'll help.

reasons.streetSmarts: You kept the moment steady instead of letting your face give anything away.
reasons.integrity: Matching Alex's excitement while sitting on this isn't neutral — it's a small performance.

choices.label: Are you sure the timing feels right?

reasons.savvy: You found a way to introduce a note of caution without revealing anything you'd promised to keep.
reasons.integrity: That question was honest, even if Alex doesn't know why you're asking it.

choices.label: I need a second — that's a lot to take in.

reasons.integrity: You didn't fake a reaction you didn't have.
reasons.streetSmarts: That pause is the kind of thing Alex might remember later and wonder about.

reveal_tense.message: Weeks later, Alex pulls you aside, grinning, unable to keep it in. "I'm going to propose. To Jordan. I want your help picking the place." You're still carrying what Jordan told you — and still a little angry about it — and it's hard to separate that from what's happening in front of you right now.

choices.label: That's incredible. Of course I'll help.

reasons.integrity: Enthusiasm you don't feel, aimed at someone who has no idea what you know, is a heavier lie than it looks like.

choices.label: Are you sure the timing feels right?

reasons.savvy: You let your discomfort show up as a real question instead of swallowing it entirely.

reasons.integrity: You didn't perform happiness you didn't have, even under pressure.
reasons.streetSmarts: That reaction is going to raise questions you can't fully answer.

jordan_returns_calm.message: Jordan finds you a few days later, quieter than usual. "I heard he's planning something. Should I tell him before he does it? Before he does something like propose?" They're asking you directly this time — no hedging.

choices.label: Yes. Before he does anything, not after.
choices.consequence: Jordan tells Alex two days later. It's a hard conversation, but it happens on Jordan's terms, before the proposal — and however it lands, it's honest.

reasons.savvy: You read that 'before' mattered more than 'gently.'
reasons.integrity: You gave the same honest answer you'd been building toward the whole time.
reasons.streetSmarts: Timing this before the proposal, not after, kept the damage as contained as it could be.

choices.label: That's your call. I can't make it for you.
choices.consequence: Jordan hesitates for another week. By the time they decide, the proposal has already happened.

reasons.integrity: Neutral wasn't dishonest, but it also wasn't the clarity Jordan was actually asking you for.

choices.label: I think you already know what you should do.
choices.consequence: Jordan nods slowly. You never find out what they decide — only that they stop mentioning it to you at all.

reasons.streetSmarts: Handing the question back protected you from the middle of it, but it also left Jordan alone with it.

jordan_returns_tense.message: Jordan corners you, tense. "I know you're angry with me. But I heard something's coming with Alex. Should I say something before it happens?" There's an edge in their voice this time — they know exactly how you feel about this.

choices.label: Yes. And you should have already.
choices.consequence: Jordan tells Alex, stung by how you said it as much as by having to say it at all. The conversation with Alex is honest. The one between you and Jordan takes much longer to recover.

reasons.integrity: The advice was right even though the delivery cost you something with Jordan directly.
reasons.streetSmarts: Being right and being kind aren't the same move, and you picked right.

choices.label: I'm still too annoyed to be objective about this.
choices.consequence: Jordan goes quiet. Neither of you brings it up again, and the proposal happens without anyone saying anything.

reasons.integrity: At least it was honest about where you actually stood.
reasons.streetSmarts: It also left Jordan with no real answer at the exact moment they needed one.

choices.label: This isn't about my anger. Tell him.
choices.consequence: Jordan tells Alex before the proposal. Your own anger takes longer to fade than the crisis itself did.

reasons.savvy: You separated your own feelings from the actual stakes for Jordan and Alex.
reasons.integrity: You gave the honest answer even while still carrying your own reaction to it.
